Hi guys, I'm trying to have unique keys with foreign key associated with one of them but I think typeorm is creating different unique keys.

Here is my model file:

```ts
import {
  Column,
  Entity,
  JoinColumn,
  OneToOne,
  PrimaryGeneratedColumn,
  Unique,
} from 'typeorm';

import { BotModel } from './bot.model';

@Entity('intent')
@Unique(['botId', 'name'])
export class IntentModel {
  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid')
  intentId: string;

  @Column()
  botId: string;

  @OneToOne(() => BotModel, { cascade: true })
  @JoinColumn({
    name: 'botId',
    referencedColumnName: 'botId',
  })
  bot: BotModel;

  @Column({ length: 16 })
  name: string;

  @Column({
    length: 128,
    nullable: true,
  })
  description: string;
}
```

My `create table intent` from mysql:

```mysql
CREATE TABLE `intent` (
  `intentId` varchar(36) NOT NULL,
  `botId` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  `description` varchar(128) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`intentId`),
  UNIQUE KEY `REL_94de4914fe0a743917de52fe8e` (`botId`),
  UNIQUE KEY `IDX_94de4914fe0a743917de52fe8e` (`botId`),
  UNIQUE KEY `IDX_78750387b2c61fb51adb75b5ab` (`botId`,`name`),
  CONSTRAINT `FK_94de4914fe0a743917de52fe8e7` FOREIGN KEY (`botId`) REFERENCES `bot` (`botId`) ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE NO ACTION
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=latin1
```

When I try to insert different name with id(already inserted) I'm getting this:
```mysql
ER_DUP_ENTRY: Duplicate entry '0b387f8b-d330-4b39-93d2-5637f11001b7' for key 'REL_94de4914fe0a743917de52fe8e'
```

I tried in different ways but no success.

This is a conceptual issue that can be verified without building or running the code.
